name: Konza Prairie and the Flint Hills
story: Konza Prairie is an 8,616-acre protected area of native tallgrass prairie located in the Flint Hills of northeastern Kansas. It features a topographically complex landscape with tallgrass, forest, and limestone outcrops. A herd of approximately 2,400 bison graze on the hills of the preserve.
matters: The site is part of the largest remaining area of unplowed tallgrass prairie in North America, serving as a natural laboratory for studying ecological patterns. Key natural processes such as periodic fire and grazing help sustain this unique grassland ecosystem.
